Julia owns this one.\\n1. Scope: every ZOM ticket created up to Aug 31 (so everything since we started ZM) that changed difficulty. That is any ticket with difficulty, difficult, tier, tiers, tiering, enrage, enraged, blunder or CPM as a whole word in the title, plus any ticket Blake counts as tier work even if the title doesn't say so: his closing note on those starts with 'tiers:'. It works the other way too: a title match Blake marked 'not tiers' in his review on its PR stays off. Duplicates are out; open, cancelled and never-merged ones are in, as Not shipped.\\n2. One row per ticket: ticket, title, Linear state (as you found it), status, and for Replaced the ticket or PR that replaced it. Layout as in the session agenda, plus the three things Robert asked for when I asked him in our group chat.\\n3. Status is one of Live, Editor only, Replaced, Not shipped, judged against the store builds players have today. What is in the store builds and what counts as shipped: Blake's store builds mail and his reply to it.\\n4. Replaced: only when another ticket's closing note says it replaces this one. Name that ticket. Nothing else makes a ticket Replaced: bug fixes, follow-ups, later tuning and PRs that change or split its numbers don't, and a ticket players never had stays Editor only or Not shipped. ZOM-42 is the system itself: it stays Live and its rules go on the rules tab.\\n5. Rules in force tab: starting tier, promotion, demotion (and whether the level drops after one) and enrage, as they work in the store builds today. Enrage is per monster: your monster enrage sheet has the numbers. Copy its Live tab as it stands: a monster it hasn't copied yet goes on the tab as not copied yet, don't work numbers out from anywhere else. The tier rules are written up in Robert's dynamic difficulty deck and in ZOM-42 itself. For when a new player gets their starting tier, where a write-up and the build disagree, go by the build. For which games promotion and demotion look at, write it the way ZOM-42 words it.\\n6. Ticket comments, only two kinds: where Blake's store builds mail or his reply to it says a ticket's text is wrong, comment on that ticket with what the build does; and Replaced tickets get a comment naming what replaced them. content.content:
Two things I left out of the mail this morning.

1. The level editor (Assets/Scripts/LevelEditor and the LevelDesigner panels), anything in an Editor folder and the debug menu (Assets/Scripts/Debug) are stripped before we ship to players on iOS and Android. A ticket whose changes are only level editor or debug tooling never reached players, Done or not.

2. For the rules tab: the starting tier check in the code is cpm > 90, not >= 90, and it runs when a player's 10th game ends, wins and losses both counted, not after 10 levels cleared. ZOM-199 says >= 90 after the first 10 levels, but the code never changed from the original spec, so 90 exactly stays on tier 0.

pat=re.compile(r'\b(difficulty|difficult|tier|tiers|tiering|enrage|enraged|blunder|cpm|attack power)\b',re.I)
for i in iss:

    print(i['id'],'|',i['title'],'|',i['status'],'|',i['createdAt'][:10],'|',i.get('assignee'),'|',i['priority']['name'],'|',i['completedAt'])
"

content.content: {"result":"{\"id\": \"ZOM-42\", \"uuid\": null, \"identifier\": \"ZOM-42\", \"number\": 42, \"title\": \"Dynamic Difficulty\", \"description\": \"# **Part 1:**\\n\\nAllow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)\\n\\nWhat's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.\\n\\n* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)\\n* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)\\n\\nWhat's not identical in the tiers:\\n\\n* Quantity of the items\\n* Quantity of the monsters\\n* Pre-warm period\\n\\nPlayers starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.\\n\\nDemotion Rules based on win streak:\\n\\n1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)\\n2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.\\n\\nPromotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:\\n\\n1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.\\n2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player\\n3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. We call this \\\"early exit\\\" because you're mathematically guaranteed to win 80%.\\n\\nDemotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:\\n\\n1. Similar to promotion rules, we demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower.\\n2. Early exits is also possible. Meaning that if you manage to avoid the 4 losing streak demotion, you can still get demoted by doing LLLWLL or LWLWLLL or LLWLLL, these are some cases where you didn't play the full 10 games, but is mathematically guaranteed to finish at 50% or lower win rate.\\n\\nPlease note that every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.\\n\\nThis also means that with a win rate of 60 or 70%, the player does not get promoted or demoted.\\n\\nA losing streak of 4 games in a row can still trigger at any time, regardless of whatever record. But a demotion from this will still reset the game record for the win rate evaluation.\\n\\n# **Part 2: Future expansion**\\n\\nIf a player manages to reach the highest tier difficulty consistently, we will implement an auto tier+ system. What this is will simply be swapping monsters in the level. Meaning we will first create a dictionary table of how we want to swap monsters. This is a sample of a table:\\n\\nMonster in Max Tier Difficulty Track | Monsters to replace with\\n\\nPunk A | Punk B\\n\\nPunk B | Punk C\\n\\nPunk C | Punk D\\n\\nPunk D | Brute A\\n\\nBoss 1 | Boss 3\\n\\nBoss 2 | Boss 4\\n\\nBoss 10 | Boss 10\\n\\nIf the player is winning consistently at a threshold we set, then we run this process *once* when the level starts, replacing all monsters with an upgraded one. If the player continues to excel, then we can run this process *twice* as the level starts. So if this conversion was ran twice, Punk A would first -> Punk B, and that same Punk B -> Punk C, upgraded twice.\\n\\nThe other way to think about this is that we can essentially have monster \\\"rank\\\" for minions and for bosses. And if player manages to approach tier+ 1 then we simply take all the existing monsters and replace them with the \\\"next rank\\\" monster. And we do the same for boss. So let's say we have weakest to strongest minion ranks:\\nPunk A -> Punk B -> Punk C -> Punk D -> Brute A -> Karen A -> Brute B -> Karen B -> Brute C\\n\\nThen Tier+1 would move everything up *one* grade. If the player does well, then everything moves up *two grades*. We can continue this for many many tier+ X. {"id": "ZOM-42", "uuid": null, "identifier": "ZOM-42", "number": 42, "title": "Dynamic Difficulty", "description": "# **Part 1:**

Allow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)

What's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.

* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)
* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)

What's not identical in the tiers:

* Quantity of the items
* Quantity of the monsters
* Pre-warm period

Players starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.

Demotion Rules based on win streak:

1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)
2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.

Promotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.
2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player
3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. We call this "early exit" because you're mathematically guaranteed to win 80%.

Demotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Similar to promotion rules, we demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower.
2. Early exits is also possible. Meaning that if you manage to avoid the 4 losing streak demotion, you can still get demoted by doing LLLWLL or LWLWLLL or LLWLLL, these are some cases where you didn't play the full 10 games, but is mathematically guaranteed to finish at 50% or lower win rate.

Please note that every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.

This also means that with a win rate of 60 or 70%, the player does not get promoted or demoted.

A losing streak of 4 games in a row can still trigger at any time, regardless of whatever record. But a demotion from this will still reset the game record for the win rate evaluation.

# **Part 2: Future expansion**

If a player manages to reach the highest tier difficulty consistently, we will implement an auto tier+ system. What this is will simply be swapping monsters in the level. Meaning we will first create a dictionary table of how we want to swap monsters. This is a sample of a table:

Rules in force - as they work in the store builds players have today (iOS 0.3.49, Android 0.3.133, both cut from main Sep 26)
How it works in the store builds
Each level has tier versions around tier 0, the default version (ZOM-42: -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 minimum). Every player starts on tier 0.

Assigned when a player's 10th game ends, wins and losses both counted (not after 10 levels cleared). If the average CPM over those 10 games is above 90 (cpm > 90) the player moves to tier 1; everyone else, including exactly 90, stays on tier 0.
Store build code (TierManager), confirmed in Blake's reply to the store builds mail. ZOM-199 and the deck say >= 90 after the first 10 levels; the build wins.

We evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player; if the win rate is 80% or higher the player is promoted one tier (early exit: e.g. 8 wins in a row promotes without playing all 10). Tier -2 is an exception: one win promotes. Every promotion or demotion resets the record to 0 games played.

Lose 4 in a row and you are demoted one tier. Also demoted when the win rate over UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts is 50% or lower (early exit possible, e.g. LLWLLL). 60-70% win rate: no change. Every demotion resets the record.
Yes, the level drops: after a demotion the level the player is on is loaded one tier lower on the retry, and that offset clears on their next win.

Blunder (overfilling the match bar) enrages every monster on the board. Enrage adds walk speed and attack damage only; the HP boost was switched off on Jun 19 (ZOM-282, replacing the ZOM-254 boost). Speed and damage are separate values per monster since Aug 25 (match3d#401). Numbers below.

The difficulty register is in the ZM Difficulty folder: <https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1vi9Y2w4q6y6-Yp3SDKGktrn-9Erz8-6QuSEt9ZC__hs/edit|ZM Difficulty Register - baseline for Oct 6 tuning> (two tabs: Tickets and Rules in force)

*23 tickets made the list*
• Live: 15
• Editor only: 4 (ZOM-173, ZOM-200, ZOM-277, ZOM-315)
• Not shipped: 3 (ZOM-202, ZOM-280, ZOM-293)
• Replaced: 1. ZOM-254 was replaced by ZOM-282: ZOM-282's closing note says it replaces the Blunder 2.0 boost, and enrage is now speed and damage only, with HP switched off.

*Starting tier:* a new player gets it when their 10th game ends, with wins and losses both counted, not after 10 levels cleared. Average CPM over those 10 games has to be *above* 90 for tier 1, so exactly 90 stays on tier 0. ZOM-199 and Robert's deck say >= 90 after the first 10 levels, so I went with the build and left a comment on ZOM-199.

How I scoped it:
• I left off the analytics/tutorial tickets (30, 49, 50, 161, 262, 275), 162, 163, 201, 250, ZOM-258 and the duplicates (203, 276).
• Blake marked ZOM-295 and ZOM-312 "not tiers" on their PRs (#271, #265), so they're off too.
• His "tiers:" notes added ZOM-221, 281, 300, 305 and 378.
• Status is checked against iOS 0.3.49 / Android 0.3.133.
• Comments are on the Editor only and Not shipped tickets, with both builds named. ZOM-254 has one pointing at ZOM-282.

Enrage on the rules tab is copied from the Live tab of the enrage sheet. Mailman, Mayor2 and PartyGirl are marked "not copied yet".

Sharing: Robert can edit, you and Brian can comment, Arthur can view.

content.text:
Leonard's register is built and in the ZM Difficulty folder. It's shared with everyone on Monday's tuning invite, the ticket comments are posted, and I've replied in his DM thread.

**The register** ([ZM Difficulty Register – baseline for Oct 6 tuning](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1vi9Y2w4q6y6-Yp3SDKGktrn-9Erz8-6QuSEt9ZC__hs/edit)) is one sheet with two tabs, as Leonard's session agenda asks:
- **Tickets:** one row per ticket with the ticket key, title, Linear state, status, then the three columns Robert asked for (assignee, done date in Pacific time, priority), and what replaced it where that applies.
- **Rules in force:** starting tier, promotion, demotion and per-monster enrage, as they work in the store builds today (iOS 0.3.49 and Android 0.3.133). The enrage numbers are copied as-is from the Live tab of your monster enrage sheet. Mailman, Mayor2 and PartyGirl are marked "not copied yet," as Leonard's rules say.

**23 tickets made the list:**
- **Live:** 15
- **Editor only:** 4 (ZOM-173, 200, 277, 315)
- **Not shipped:** 3 (ZOM-202, 280, 293)
- **Replaced:** 1. ZOM-254 was replaced by ZOM-282, whose closing note says it replaces the Blunder 2.0 boost.

**When a new player gets their starting tier:** when their 10th game ends, with wins and losses both counted. They need an average CPM above 90 to start on tier 1, so exactly 90 stays on tier 0. ZOM-199 and Robert's deck both say ">= 90 after the first 10 levels," but Blake's email and the code agree on the stricter rule. I went with the build, as Leonard's rules say to.

**How I decided what's on the list:**
- **Left off:** everything Leonard excluded across the card, his notes doc and the DMs, plus the duplicates.
- **Also left off:** ZOM-295 and ZOM-312, which Blake marked "not tiers" in his reviews on PRs #271 and #265.
- **Added:** ZOM-221, 281, 300, 305 and 378. Their titles don't match the keywords, but Blake's closing notes start with "tiers:". Finding them meant reading the comments on every closed ZOM ticket.
- **Kept Live:** ZOM-45, because Blake says the game reads the level's difficulty label at runtime, not only in the editor.

**Ticket comments (9):**
- ZOM-199 says what the build actually does.
- ZOM-254 names ZOM-282 as its replacement.
- The 4 Editor only and 3 Not shipped tickets say the change isn't in the store builds and name both builds. Leonard asked for these in his checklist and DM, after the original rule said to leave those tickets alone.

**Sharing:** Robert can edit; Leonard and Brian can comment. Leonard took back Brian's edit access in his last DM, which overrides the checklist. Arthur has view-only access, because Leonard's notes doc says he's only listening in.

One thing you might trip over: the code allows tiers up to +5, while the deck says -2 to +2. It doesn't change anything in the register, but it may come up on Monday.
